title: A rail map's rails: res/field/rails/<n>.json
description: Rail file n of ARCID_RAIL_HEADERS (a/0/7/8), which a header of headers.json names: the points, lines, cameras and curves that FieldRailLoader_LoadFile loads for the rail system (field_rail.c), and the tiles of each line, which FieldRailTilemap_Load reads from the archive's file n plus the count of rail files (rail_attr.c). Lines, points, cameras and curves are named by their place in their lists, from 0, and null is RAIL_ID_NONE. tools/data/rail_data.py packs them in order.

tile_width.description: The width of a tile, in 4096ths of a unit, which turns rail positions into world positions (RailDataHandle's tileWidth)

name.description: The rail editor's name of the point, which the code doesn't read; padded with spaces

position.description: Where the point is, in 4096ths of a unit

camera.description: The camera of cameras that applies at the point, and that the blending cameras of its lines start or end at (GetRailCameraByPoint)

lines.description: The four slots of the lines that meet here (RAIL_POINT_LINE_MAX)

line.description: The line, of lines, or null for an empty slot

dir.description: The direction the line leaves the point in

width.description: The rail's width at the point on this line, which a line's width blends between from end to end (GetLerpedLineWidthByLineYPos)

lines.description: The lines between points (RailLine), with their tiles

name.description: The rail editor's name of the line, which the code doesn't read; padded with NULs

point_a.description: The point the line starts at

point_b.description: The point the line ends at

dir.description: The direction along the line from point_a to point_b

curve.description: The curve of curves that bends the line

camera.description: The camera of cameras that applies on the line

tiles.description: The line's tilemap (RailTilemap), a row for each tile along the line from point_a, each row the tiles across it from one side to the other, as many as the rail is wide; FieldRailTilemap_GetTileAtPos reads the tile at a rail position. Each tile is a map tile type in hex: its flags (TILE_FLAG_* in include/field/field_map.h, GetTileFlags) in the high 16 bits and its class (TILE_CLASS_*, GetTileClass) in the low 16

cameras.description: The cameras of the points and lines (RailCamera)

function.description: The camera function, of RAIL_CAMERA_CURVE_FUNC_SET in rail_data_handle.c, which field_rail_func.c defines. RailCameraFuncSetStaticPYR puts the eye at params 0 to 2 from the unit the camera follows; RailCameraFuncSetStaticPYDist and FieldRailCamera_FixedAngleAtCentre set the pitch, yaw and distance from params 0 to 2, and FieldRailCamera_FixedAngleShift and _FixedAngleShiftAtFocus also offset the target by params 3 to 5; FieldRailCamera_FixedEyeTarget puts the eye at params 0 to 2 and the target at 3 to 5; FieldRailCamera_Orbit orbits the target at params 2 to 4 at angle param 0 and distance param 1, and FieldRailCamera_OrbitMovingPoint moves the target to params 5 to 7 along the line; FieldRailCamera_YawFromPoint sets the pitch and distance from params 0 and 1 and faces from the point at X param 2 and Z param 3; the FollowHeading functions face along the line, adding param 0 to its yaw, with pitch param 1 (added to the slope's by FieldRailCamera_FollowHeadingSlope) and distance param 2. The Blend functions blend the parameters of the cameras of the line's two points as these read them, and FieldRailCamera_ApplyLineStart and _ApplyLineEnd apply the camera of the line's first or second point, without reading their own.

params.description: The function's eight parameters, as the function reads them: angles in 65536ths of a turn, distances and positions in 4096ths of a unit

kind.description: The conversion between rail and world positions, of RAIL_CONV_RAIL_TO_WORLD_FUNCS and RAIL_CONV_WORLD_TO_RAIL_FUNCS: RailMath_RailToWorldNoCurve for a straight line, or an arc around the center on the X-Z plane, or one that also rises along Y (RailMath_RailToWorldSlerpXZ, _SlerpXYZ)

center.description: The center of the arc, in 4096ths of a unit

unk10.description: Bytes that the code doesn't read
